name: Salt
flavor: Clean, direct saltiness with no sweetness, acidity, heat, or aroma. Intensifies savory flavors but can easily make the dip too salty.

name: White sesame seeds
flavor: Mildly nutty with a delicate seed crunch. Toasting increases the roasted aroma; unroasted seeds are gentler.

name: Sichuan pepper
thai_name: พริกไทยเสฉวน
flavor: Citrusy, floral aroma and a distinctive tingling, numbing sensation. The numbing effect differs from chili heat.

name: Homemade soy sauce
flavor: For this station, homemade soy sauce means dark soy sauce: deep soy savoriness, dark color, and a rounded, sometimes molasses-like sweetness. Saltiness and sweetness vary with the recipe.

name: Cilantro
flavor: Fresh, leafy, citrusy herbal aroma. Some diners perceive it as soapy. Here this means larger leaf pieces, distinct from the finely chopped option.

name: Barbecue sauce
thai_name: ซอสบาร์บีคิวจีน
flavor: Shacha sauce (Chinese barbecue sauce): savory, roasted, oily, and aromatic, with deep umami and seafood notes. This condiment is confirmed to be shacha, rather than a sweet barbecue sauce.

name: Minced pork
flavor: Meaty savoriness, mild pork sweetness, soft small pieces, and some richness from fat. Assumed fully cooked and only lightly seasoned.

name: Ground chili
flavor: Bright chili heat with fresh, grassy pepper notes and a moist texture. Assumed fresh crushed chili without added salt or vinegar.

name: Lime juice
flavor: Sharp, fresh sourness with a citrus aroma. Adds brightness and cuts through oily or rich ingredients.

name: Vinegar
thai_name: น้ำส้มสายชู
flavor: Direct sourness with an acetic aroma, less fresh citrus fragrance than lime. Assumed plain vinegar; rice or dark vinegar would add different notes.

name: Crushed peanuts
thai_name: ถั่วลิสงบด
flavor: Roasted nuttiness, mild natural sweetness, and a coarse crunch. Adds body and richness; assumed roasted and unsalted.

name: Thai chicken sauce
thai_name: น้ำจิ้มไก่
flavor: Sweet first, then gently tangy and mildly spicy, with garlic notes. Its thick, concentrated sugar syrup adds sweetness, gloss, viscosity, and body, thickening the dip.

name: Sesame oil blend
thai_name: น้ำมันงาผสม
flavor: Nutty sesame aroma and a smooth, oily mouthfeel. Assumed a toasted sesame oil blend; aroma strength depends on the blend.

name: Crushed garlic
thai_name: กระเทียมบด
flavor: Strong raw garlic pungency, sharp sulfurous aroma, and a fine moist texture that spreads through the dip.

name: Chilli powder
flavor: Dry chili heat with earthy, sometimes roasted notes and a fine, slightly gritty texture. Assumed ground dried chili without a seasoning blend.

name: Sesame sauce
flavor: Rich roasted sesame nuttiness, thick creamy body, and a slight bitter edge. Assumed sesame-paste-based sauce; added salt or sugar varies.

name: Fried garlic
thai_name: กระเทียมเจียว
flavor: Toasty, mellow garlic aroma, light sweetness, and crisp texture. Less raw pungency than fresh garlic; may carry some frying oil.

name: Fermented bean curd
thai_name: เต้าหู้ยี้
flavor: Concentrated saltiness, fermented funk, deep savoriness, and a soft creamy texture. Red and white varieties may differ in sweetness and aroma.

name: Fish sauce
flavor: Intense saltiness and fermented fish umami with a distinctive aroma. Small amounts add savory depth familiar in many Thai dips.

name: Oyster sauce
flavor: Rounded savory umami, moderate saltiness, some sweetness, and a thick glossy texture. Oyster intensity varies by brand.

name: Chili oil
thai_name: น้ำมันพริก
flavor: Chili heat in an oily base, often with toasted chili aroma. Adds richness; assumed no pronounced Sichuan-pepper numbness unless specified.

name: Mala oil sauce
flavor: Chili heat plus Sichuan-pepper tingling and numbness in an oily sauce, with savory spices. Adds both richness and a numbing sensation; intensity depends on the sauce.

name: Flavoured bean sauce
thai_name: เต้าซี่ปรุงรส
flavor: A Lao Gan Ma-style seasoned fermented black bean condiment: salty, deeply savory umami, fermented bean aroma, and soft bean pieces. Oil, chili heat, and roasted aromatics depend on the variety; do not assume it is the chili-crisp variant.

name: Shiitake sauce
flavor: Finely minced shiitake mushrooms in oil: distinctly salty and savory, with a pronounced shiitake aroma, small mushroom pieces, and an oily texture. Adds mushroom umami and richness rather than a smooth creamy body.

name: Garlic
flavor: Raw garlic pungency and a sharp sulfurous aroma with a firm bite. Here this means small fresh garlic pieces, distinct from crushed garlic and fried garlic.

name: Minced shallots
flavor: The station label Minced shallots refers to chopped scallions (green onions), not bulb shallots. Fresh green onion aroma, gentle onion pungency, a little sweetness, and a light crisp bite.

name: Parsley
flavor: The station label Parsley refers to finely chopped cilantro (coriander), not European parsley. Fresh, citrusy, leafy herbal aroma distributed through the dip by fine chopping; some diners perceive cilantro as soapy.

name: Sugar
flavor: Clean sweetness with no acidity, saltiness, heat, or aroma. Fine sugar grains dissolve into the dip, softening sourness and balancing salty seasonings; too much makes the sauce cloying.
